audit_findings.title: Acquisition-fed growth may be capitalized without its acquisition cost
audit_findings.mechanism: Forecast growth and owner earnings would be overstated if achieving 6%-8% growth requires recurring acquisition spending excluded from OE.
audit_findings.evidence: These companies collectively contributed approximately $168.3 million in sales for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to $73.1 million in the same period last year.
audit_findings.explanation: No present error is demonstrated. Acquired operations are already within the owned perimeter, while the latest 10-Q reports organic growth of 6.8% for first-half 2026 and 12.4% for the second quarter, supporting at least the base growth rate without current acquisitions. The risk becomes active if future organic growth falls short and acquisitions are needed to deliver the modeled path.
audit_findings.action: Build a constant-perimeter OE series and track organic OE growth quarterly; rerun the DCF with recurring acquisition investment deducted only if the forecast cannot be achieved organically.

audit_findings.title: Contingent purchase-price liability may be missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $3.318 million remaining non-competition consideration, equal to $0.42 per diluted share and 0.25% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any acquisition consideration not already charged through equity-level OE should be deducted in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The fair value of the liability for the contingent consideration payments recognized at December 31, 2025 totaled approximately $5.3 million out of the remaining potential payments of $7.3 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The specific $5.25 million earn-out outstanding at year-end 2025 was paid during first-half 2026, and the June 2026 earn-out balance is zero; the valuation's June cash balance is therefore already after that payment. A separate $3.318 million present-value liability for acquisition-related non-competition payments remains, but even full omission changes base value by only about $0.42 per share and cannot alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether future non-competition payments are already captured in OE; if not, deduct $3.318 million from the bridge, with no broader operating rerun required.

audit_findings.title: Acquired-intangible depletion may have been stripped as noncash D&A
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $9.8 million FY2025 amortization, equal to 12.5% of the $78.7 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back acquired-intangible amortization without an economic replacement charge raises anchor OE and every forecast and terminal cash flow derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: Amortization expense related to intangible assets was approximately $ 9.8 million, $ 6.7 million, and $ 4.4 million for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a large and rising amortization charge, but the record does not establish whether the OE calculation added it all back or whether maintenance capex, customer-development expense, or another charge captures depletion of acquired relationships and technology. At 12.5% of anchor OE, a substantial uncaptured replacement cost is reasonably capable of materially changing value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the OE addback between $9.4 million physical depreciation and $9.8 million intangible amortization, estimate maintenance spending needed to preserve acquired customer and technology earnings, and rerun all scenarios with that economic charge.

audit_findings.title: The anchor tax rate contains discrete benefits
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $11.223 million FY2025 free-trade-zone tax reduction, equal to 14.3% of anchor OE; discrete refund and vesting benefits unquantified; effective rate was 17.2% in FY2025 versus 20.2% in first-half 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: An abnormally low anchor tax burden increases OE, while assuming temporary jurisdictional benefits persist increases forecast and terminal cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: The decrease in the effective tax rate for the current period as compared to the prior period is largely due to a shift in mix or pre-tax income to jurisdictions where we are taxed at a favorable rate as well as increased discrete tax benefits associated with vested equity and a state tax refund.
audit_findings.explanation: The presence of discrete benefits is demonstrated, although their individual amounts are not disclosed. The 2026 effective-rate increase confirms that FY2025 was not fully representative. Separately, the filed free-trade-zone benefit is large enough that its duration and conditions are material to terminal value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the state-refund and equity-vesting tax amounts and the expiration and renewal terms of the foreign tax incentives; normalize anchor taxes and rerun the DCF using a documented long-run tax rate.

audit_findings.title: A material transient labor cost remains in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: filed more than $6.3 million pretax, a gross amount equal to approximately 8.0% of the $78.7 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Removing a resolved cost raises anchor OE; leaving it in the anchor while also modeling its recovery as growth understates the anchor but may overstate forecast growth.
audit_findings.evidence: We estimate that the AJR Labor Issue added over $6.3 million in incremental labor cost to our cost-of-sales for year ended December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The incremental FY2025 cost is demonstrated and large enough to affect value materially. Improved 2026 gross margins and operating efficiencies suggest some recovery, but the filing does not quantify how much ceased or became ordinary labor cost, so the correct normalization and interaction with growth remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile AJR labor inefficiency by quarter through 2026, identify the portion eliminated versus recurring, and rerun anchor OE and growth assumptions together to prevent either omission or double counting.

audit_findings.title: The equity-method joint venture is not reconciled to stakes_net of zero
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $6.667 million carrying value at June 2026, equal to $0.84 per diluted share and 0.51% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The investment should either contribute distributable OE within the operating DCF or be removed from OE and added as a separately valued stake in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: For one joint venture where the Company is not the primary beneficiary, the joint venture is not consolidated and is accounted for under the equity method.
audit_findings.explanation: The reconciliation is missing, but scale is not material. The venture produced only $0.119 million of net equity-method earnings in 2025 and a $0.010 million net loss after basis amortization in first-half 2026, while distributing $0.250 million. Even treating the entire $6.667 million carrying value as omitted would change base value by only about $0.84 per share.
audit_findings.action: Trace equity-method earnings, basis amortization, and distributions through OE; retain distributable OE in operations or exclude it and add an independently supported stake value, avoiding double counting.
